name: Create a model
description: A competitor naming a model and the GitHub repository it will be published from. THE REPOSITORY IS THE KEY -- one entry per repository per owner -- and it is normalised by repo_path() before anything else looks at it, so a pasted browser URL, an ssh remote and a bare `owner/name` are one value in the column and a stored URL can never be pasted back into a release URL. The path's first segment must be the caller's own GitHub login, which is what users.handle IS, or an organisation the season allows: a competitor may not enter someone else's repository, and the check is at creation because the repository is the entry's and never a submission's. Write, then diagnose: the insert carries every rule as a predicate so a refusal is a row that was never written, and `why` reads back which one it was. A model is created empty -- creating one enters nothing and starts no clock; POST /v1/submissions is what puts a release under it.

tasks.name: A name and a repository, declared

logic.detail: name is what you call this model; url is the GitHub repository it is published from, as a URL or as owner/name.

input.query: INSERT INTO models (owner_id, game_id, name, repo) SELECT ($1)::uuid, g.id, btrim(($3)::text), repo_path(($4)::text) FROM games g JOIN live_sessions ls ON ls.sid = ($5)::uuid AND ls.user_id = ($1)::uuid LEFT JOIN seasons s ON s.game_id = g.id AND s.closed_at IS NULL WHERE g.slug = ($2)::text AND repo_path(($4)::text) IS NOT NULL AND btrim(($3)::text) <> '' AND length(btrim(($3)::text)) <= 64 AND (s.id IS NULL OR season_admits(s, ($1)::uuid)) AND (s.id IS NULL OR season_admits_repo(s, ($1)::uuid, ($4)::text)) AND (s.id IS NULL OR season_admits_entry(s, ($1)::uuid)) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM models e WHERE e.owner_id = ($1)::uuid AND e.game_id = g.id AND (lower(e.repo) = lower(repo_path(($4)::text)) OR lower(e.name) = lower(btrim(($3)::text))))

SELECT json_build_object( 'repo', repo_path(($3)::text), 'participant', s.id IS NULL OR season_admits(s, ($2)::uuid), 'owned', s.id IS NULL OR season_admits_repo(s, ($2)::uuid, ($3)::text), 'room', s.id IS NULL OR season_admits_entry(s, ($2)::uuid), 'entries_max', (s.rules -> 'entries' ->> 'max_per_user')::int, 'entries_used', (SELECT count(*) FROM models e WHERE e.owner_id = ($2)::uuid AND e.game_id = g.id AND e.retired_at IS NULL), 'handle', (SELECT u.handle FROM users u WHERE u.id = ($2)::uuid), 'repo_taken', EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM models e WHERE e.owner_id = ($2)::uuid AND e.game_id = g.id AND lower(e.repo) = lower(repo_path(($3)::text))), 'name_taken', EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM models e WHERE e.owner_id = ($2)::uuid AND e.game_id = g.id AND lower(e.name) = lower(btrim(($4)::text)))) AS body FROM games g LEFT JOIN seasons s ON s.game_id = g.id AND s.closed_at IS NULL WHERE g.slug = ($1)::text

tasks.name: That is not a repository
tasks.description: repo_path() answers NULL for anything that is not exactly one repository -- a releases URL, a tree URL, a bare word -- so this is a 400 about what was typed and never a 409 about a rule.

mappings.logic: url must name one GitHub repository: https://github.com/you/your-model, or you/your-model. A releases or tree URL names a page inside one, not the repository itself.

input.query: SELECT json_build_object('model_id', e.id, 'model', e.name, 'repo', e.repo, 'game', g.slug, 'owner', u.handle, 'created_at', e.created_at, 'versions', '[]'::json) AS body FROM models e JOIN games g ON g.id = e.game_id JOIN users u ON u.id = e.owner_id JOIN live_sessions s ON s.sid = ($4)::uuid AND s.user_id = e.owner_id WHERE e.owner_id = ($1)::uuid AND g.slug = ($2)::text AND lower(e.repo) = lower(repo_path(($3)::text))
